en: At the sight he plunged toward the grave
Great Bilgich was utterly spent
Escaping the snare by guile
He opened his mouth wide
Crossing the open plain
He braced and rose to his feet
His tack worn from the flight
Across the flat beyond the hills
Passing through the hands of many troops
In this wretched world
The land lay divided
He drove on with all his soul
He fled toward Beijing
There were stretched iron nets
Would the Chinese not seize him from afar
A cause intervened and stopped him
He was distraught when his warrior fell
The gray-wolf hero’s wound
Ak Joltoy, his surviving elder
Grieving and tearing up the ground
Restoring his sobbing life
When his destined hour comes, he truly lies down
Does this head not meet its end
Lead him out from the perilous side
Do not let the forty falter; behold the cauldron
The eighteen thousand worlds
The black earth swallows utterly
This world in which he dwells
This fleeting world beneath the moon
Every person in the world
Cannot remain forever, my kinsman
The peerless hero in this world
As fate closes his eyes
So spoke warrior Seytek
Beginning many words of counsel
There he remained thereafter
Muraaly’s destined fortune
Let us begin the tale with news of Bilgich
Great Bilgich, who had been wounded
Struggled along his road
All one hundred champions
Had lost to the Kyrgyz warriors
Meeting death together
Great Bilgich traveled on again
He went along in agitation
Wounded and exhausted
When he had departed Beijing
The champion standing guard
Without being seen by the guard
With a great commotion between them
At the frontier of great Beijing
Seen indeed like Muraaly
Seytek’s kinsman Muraaly
Do not ask about Muraaly
Rich as the four plane trees
When he granted the uplands
In the contest raised by his wrath
Seytek kept it in mind
His anger took many forms then
Great Kiten lay thinking
That hero of Seytek
Among thousands in the age he was the best
He became the great father of the Chinese
No person could pass the barrier
He let no living soul escape
He made the great battlefield his land
Chongubay became a lion-like hero
He took shelter by the blue well
Fearless, never forgetting the fortress
He sprang like a blue tiger
Giving no khans room to mount
Never forgetting the fortress of the fearful
The Chinese heroes came face to face
Among the forty kinds of Chinese people
None remained when Kalcha attacked
No livestock remained to turn back
No soul remained to speak to Kalcha
They fled and were drained
Taking the road in anger
The hero came in wrath
He could not be contained beneath the blue sky
Crushing the mottled enemy
That hero, great Kiten
Seytek poured forth, destroying
He drove the enemies onward
His blue fury was unleashed
He wrapped himself in smoking blue flame
The drawn bow would not slacken
For many days and many nights
His grief did not subside
Tirelessly they shod the horse
It happened by his free will
If a living soul reached China
The road allowed no disappearance
If it bent, the road turned aside
He began the youth’s wrath
He hardened himself and spared no life
Taking revenge, he cleared the people’s road
Kiten broke down and abandoned it
He did what he knew to do
At forty he raged
Understanding much that he knew
Heroes matured in wisdom
What manner of warriors were these
Champions among the warrior people
Many steadfast souls
They never turned their faces away
For this, many went to Beijing
One wise soul devoted himself
A troublesome man descended from great Bilgich
No one dared pass through
A gray-wolf hero appeared
Saying Kiten himself was the warrior
He understood every living soul
Forty warriors answered his battle cry
Speaking more than eyes could take in
He descended upon the Kalmyks
Not one soul crossed the barrier
A troublesome man from great Bilgich
There was none he did not take
A man who brought calamity from the ravine
None escaped punishment
He mounted Kulansur
He delivered a severe punishment
From the many arrivals came his distress
He drove the exhausted Chinese
He watched while striking the herds
He gathered them all like this
His venom was carefully hidden within
Such calamities existed in Kakan
What pure justice was there
Saying Bilgich lay behind the encirclement
Halting across the whole world
There was no end to the Chinese
If the world broke without stopping
If the people suffered calamity
He would not care though all went awry
All of the world beneath the moon
That fierce Kiten beneath the moon
He counted it as no more than his boot tip
He gave no thought to the right or to torment
Poor Kiten grew agitated
His son was Khan Kalcha
The wrathful Kuronchu
Of the fierce Joltoy
What answer could there be
The four corners of the world
He breathed fire like a blast
While Kiten remained above
At that time great Bilgich
Could not restrain his wrath
Warrior Bilgich who came from Kakan
Bilgich, a lion skilled with the spear
His fortune had been complete
He charged and struck toward Kiten
Calling Bilgich his equal then
He did not return along the road
He struck and turned with sure aim
When the wind blew from the valley
When stars covered the sky
The earth convulsed and flowed
Calmed his troubled heart
Calling out to his Chinese host
His fierce bearing settled
What he had resolved in his thoughts
The black belt drawn straight
If only he now knew, he said
There was no person who knew
Asking what had happened to the people
He was the sense of your people
This was Beijing’s great quarrel
He was khan of the gathered people
He was a support to the craftsmen
He cried out and sat in grief
Many days passed after that
A roaring giant bright as a mirror
Of the forty-tribe Chinese people
He alone was their strength
Riding horses weary across the land
Pursuing horses and tracking trails
He crossed seven river valleys
They called him a perfect mighty warrior
Upon hearing such news
He crossed the broad country
Why had his champion set out
He had not paused to inquire
Though driven in darkness
The road became a place of encounter
His forces were arranged in four
From outside an evil rear guard formed
He was a khan who endured wrath
He gathered them all firmly
He himself stood within the chain
Amid enemies like blue hell
The young hero’s forelock
The understanding of the elders
To send scouts against him
To gather news from thousands
His departure was reported to Kiten
Great Bilgich was a noble khan
Making the born warriors rejoice
Bringing ruin upon true enemies
He was a lion-like champion
He was khan of forty Chinese tribes
All forty tribes
Were the venom of a fearsome people
They praised the finest by mouth
And spoke of deeds done wisely
His temperament was settled in wisdom
It was great Bilgich himself
Of your court and Chinese people
Of the Black Kalmyks and Manchus
Working by every means
He alone had been their pillar
To all of these people
He was the falcon born among them
One who would not abandon his station
The scion of a royal palace
Great Bilgich with his thousands
His voice sounded of death
While he spoke in this way
The darkness of torment
Mourning great Bilgich
All the people’s herds were there
Bilgich who came to the gate
When poor Kiten asked
He surrendered a life like a sleeve
All the champions went together
He told the news at once
This was the lion-like hero
The khan’s healer struggled
If you are noble Kiten
Know that we have spoken much
Receive news of great Bilgich
May God not make you see it
The day itself had been ruined
The Chinese hearts constricted
A hundred champions fell into death
All the people suffered from the wicked enemy
From the people scattered in ruin
Their land darkened and collapsed
Receiving wounds in seven places
Fading away from life
My lord, the noble hero is wounded
Turning his face toward grief
Bilgich comes on in this state
From the hands of China’s enemy
My poor people have suffered
Strength left great Bilgich
Blood flowed from his wrathful side
Gathering what courage remained
A spear struck into his body
In turmoil the spear was torn free
Of the fiercely wrathful Kyrgyz
From the enemy and from Bilgich
Ak Joltoy remained alone
